## GovernanceContextBase interface

Governance state shared by every deployment, whichever approval channel it does or does not have.

Both arms of [GovernanceContext](./runtime.governancecontext.md) extend this, so the machine-wide policy and the per-key resolver are declared once and the two arms cannot drift.

**Signature:**

```typescript
interface GovernanceContextBase
```

</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Optional resolver for the policy attached to the authenticated API key.

The host policy is machine-wide and can be bound once; \*which\* key policy applies depends on who authenticated, so it is resolved per caller from the key id (see [resolveGovernanceForRequest()](./runtime.resolvegovernanceforrequest.md)<!-- -->). When omitted, or when the key has no policy of its own, the host policy alone governs.

A key policy can only ever tighten the host policy, so this never widens what a deployment allows — including which calls reach an approval gate.
